figures.caption: Figure 1. Conventional vs. proposed deepfake detection. Existing methods rely primarily on a single visual encoder and produce a binary prediction. The proposed framework fuses complementary visual, semantic, and frequency streams under an uncertaintyaware fusion to generate calibrated and explainable predictions.
Table 1. Representative features and predicates used in the proposed approach. Full list in Supplementary 6.A.

Figure 2. Overview of the proposed framework. A frozen CLIP backbone with layer-norm tuning produces Evvis. A semantic stream evaluates differentiable FACS-grounded predicates over the semantic descriptor fsem to produce Evsem. A structural stream learns four pairs of class-conditioned structural equation models, producing Evstruc. The three streams are fused by EDL into a calibrated decision with epistemic uncertainty u.
Table 3. Comparison of frame-level AUC (%) across five datasets under a cross-dataset evaluation protocol, with training performed on FF++ (c23). Best in bold and second-best underlined.
Table 4. Comparison of video-level AUC (%) across five datasets under a cross-dataset evaluation protocol, with training performed on FF++ (c23). Best in bold and second-best underlined.

Figure 4. Per-prediction outputs on correctly detected fake samples. (a) Confident cases (u = 0.07, 0.05) with strong, consistent evidence across all three streams. (b) Uncertain cases (u = 0.50, 0.48) where one stream diverges from the others, and IBDC elevates u.
